title: Characterization of Blood Outgrowth Endothelial Cells (BOEC) from Porcine Peripheral Blood
protocol: Prepare materials for collecting porcine peripheral blood.
Dilute heparin solution to 100 U/mL in sterile saline.
Add 3-4 mL of diluted heparin solution to each of two 50 mL conical tubes and two 60 mL syringes.
Draw undiluted heparin solution (1,000 U/mL) into an extension tube.
Connect a 19 G needle to one end of the heparin-filled extension tube and a heparin-containing 60 mL syringe to the other end.
Administer atropine (0.05 mg/kg), tiletamine/zolazepam (2-5 mg/kg), and xylazine (2 mg/kg) by IM injection to induce anesthesia.
Ensure adequate anesthesia once the animal is unconscious with non-rigid mandibular muscles.
Lay the pig in a supine position and place rolled-up towels on both sides for stability.
Apply an ophthalmic ointment to the eyes to prevent dryness while under anesthesia.
Provide thermal support during anesthesia using blankets, heating pads, or a heated procedure table.
Clean the femoral groin area with betadine scrub solution.
Puncture the femoral vein or artery with the 19 G needle and slowly draw 50 mL of blood into the syringe.
Draw blood slowly to avoid damaging cells.
Kink the extension tube and disconnect the 60 mL syringe immediately after drawing blood.
Transfer the blood to a heparin-containing 50 mL conical tube slowly.
Cap the 50 mL conical tube tightly, invert gently to mix, and place on ice.
Connect the remaining heparin-containing 60 mL syringe to the extension tube and unkink it.
Draw an additional 50 mL of blood into the syringe.
Remove the needle from the artery or vein immediately after drawing the blood.
Transfer the remaining blood from the extension tube into the 60 mL syringe slowly.
Disconnect the 60 mL syringe from the extension tube and transfer the blood to a heparin-containing 50 mL conical tube.
Cap the 50 mL conical tube tightly, invert gently to mix, and place on ice.
Apply pressure hemostasis to the pig's femoral groin area.
Recover the pig according to Institutional policies.
Monitor the animal continuously until it regains sufficient consciousness to maintain sternal recumbency.
Transfer the pig to its regular housing/kennel area when fully recovered.
Dilute the blood 1:1 with phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) in four 50 mL conical tubes.
Add 25 mL of room temperature ready-to-use density gradient solution to eight 50 mL conical tubes.
Very slowly pipette 25 mL of blood/saline solution along the inside of each density gradient solution containing 50 mL conical tube by holding the tube at a sharp angle to the pipette tip.
Centrifuge the tubes for 30 min at 560 x g and room temperature (RT).
Use a thin pipette to carefully collect the buffy coat from each tube and distribute evenly into two new 50 mL conical tubes.
Discard the density gradient solution containing tubes.
Make a stock solution of human plasma fibronectin by diluting it to 1 mg/mL in sterile water.
Store the aliquots at -20 °C.
Make 3.6 mL of a working solution of fibronectin by diluting 600 µL of fibronectin stock solution in 3 mL of PBS.
Transfer 600 µL of the fibronectin working solution into each well of a 6-well plate and gently rock until evenly coated.
Wait 30 min for the fibronectin to coat the wells and gently aspirate the solution out of each well.
Top up the tubes with up to 45 mL of PBS.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 560 x g and 4 °C with low brake.
Aspirate the supernatant from both tubes.
Resuspend each cell pellet in 25 mL of PBS.
Repeat to wash a second time.
Wash the cells by topping up tubes with PBS and centrifuging for 5 min at 560 x g and 4 °C with low brake.
Aspirate the supernatant from both tubes.
Resuspend each cell pellet in 25 mL of PBS and repeat to wash a second time.
Add 15 mL of 0.8% ammonium chloride solution to each tube.
Incubate on ice for 10 min.
Wash the cells by topping up tubes with PBS and centrifuging for 5 min at 560 x g and 4 °C with low brake.
Aspirate the supernatant from both tubes.
Resuspend each cell pellet in 25 mL of PBS and repeat to wash a second time.
Resuspend each cell pellet in 6 mL of EGM-2 culture medium supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) and 1x antibiotic/antimycotic solution.
Gently transfer 2 mL of the cell suspension to each well of the fibronectin-coated 6-well plate.
Gently rock until evenly coated.
Incubate the cells at 37 °C, 5% CO₂, and 100% humidity.
Gently add 1 mL of fresh culture medium to each well on the next day.
Perform a half culture medium change by gently aspirating 1.5 mL of culture medium from each well and replacing it with 1.5 mL of fresh culture medium on the subsequent day.
Gently perform a full culture medium change to each well (2 mL of fresh culture medium per well) on each of the next 5 days.
Gently change the culture medium three times per week after that.
Regularly visualize cell cultures under low power light microscopy using a 4x objective lens.
Passage BOECs into a fibronectin-coated T-75 flask when ~70%-80% confluent and continue changing culture medium three times per week.
